references.text: Isaiah prophesies about the people's spiritual blindness and deafness, where eyes see but do not understand, and ears hear but do not perceive - the same theme of God's people lacking spiritual understanding
The Lord has poured out over you a spirit of deep sleep and closed their eyes - parallel to God not giving them hearts to understand or eyes to see
Ezekiel speaks about a rebellious people who have eyes to see but do not see, and ears to hear but do not hear - a direct parallel to the spiritual condition of the people
Jeremiah speaks about a foolish people without understanding, who have eyes but do not see, and ears but do not hear
Paul quotes this verse and shows that God gave them a spirit of stupor, eyes that do not see and ears that do not hear, right up to this day
Jesus explains why he speaks in parables and quotes Isaiah about the people who see but do not perceive, and hear but do not understand
Paul quotes Isaiah about the people's hardened heart, deaf ears, and closed eyes - the same spiritual blindness that Moses describes
John quotes Isaiah saying that God has blinded their eyes and hardened their hearts, so they cannot see or understand
The Lord hardened Pharaoh's heart to display his signs - an earlier example of God controlling people's spiritual receptivity
